label: Adviser, firm and FCA authorisation stated
description: Did the adviser introduce themselves by name, name the firm, and state that the firm is authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority?

label: Call recording and data use disclosed
description: Did the adviser disclose that the call is recorded and explain in broad terms how the customer's information will be used?

label: Scope of service made clear (whole of market or panel)
description: Did the adviser explain the range of mortgages the advice covers — whole of market, a limited panel, or a single lender? MCOB 4.4A requires the customer to know the breadth of the service before advice is given.

label: Advised basis made clear
description: Did the adviser make clear that this is advised (a recommendation is being made), rather than an execution-only or information-only service?

label: Broker fee disclosed: amount, when payable, refundable
description: Did the adviser state any fee the customer will pay, how much it is, at what point it becomes payable, and whether it is refundable? A fee that only surfaces later in the process is a Consumer Duty and MCOB 4.4A failure, even if the amount is correct.

label: Lender commission / procuration fee disclosed
description: Did the adviser disclose that the firm will or may receive a commission or procuration fee from the lender?

label: Data sharing explained and customer agreement obtained
description: Did the adviser explain that the customer's information will be shared with lenders and third parties for the purpose of the application AND obtain a clear affirmative from the customer? The customer's agreement must be given explicitly and must not be inferred from silence.

label: Needs and circumstances established before any recommendation
description: Did the adviser build a picture of what the customer needs and why — purchase or remortgage, property, timescales, priorities — BEFORE recommending a product? The need must be established, not assumed from the enquiry.

label: Income, employment and expenditure captured
description: Did the adviser establish income, employment basis (employed, self-employed, contract) and regular expenditure in enough detail to support an affordability view?

label: Existing credit commitments captured
description: Did the adviser ask about existing debts and credit commitments — loans, cards, car finance, other borrowing?

label: Deposit or available equity established
description: Did the adviser establish the deposit amount and its source (or the available equity on a remortgage)?

label: Credit history explored
description: Did the adviser ask about credit history — missed payments, defaults, CCJs or other adverse credit — before recommending a lender?

label: Foreseeable changes in circumstances explored
description: Did the adviser ask about known or likely future changes that would affect affordability over the term — retirement, a planned income change, starting a family, reduced hours?

label: Term extending into retirement addressed
description: Where the recommended term runs to or beyond the customer's expected retirement age, did the adviser address how the mortgage will remain affordable in retirement? Mark not applicable only where the term clearly ends well before retirement.

label: Repayment method rationale given
description: Did the adviser explain and justify the repayment method — capital repayment versus interest-only — rather than defaulting to one? Where interest-only is recommended, a credible and stated repayment strategy is required (MCOB 11.6.41).

label: Term rationale given
description: Did the adviser explain why the recommended term was chosen, and the trade-off between a longer term (lower monthly payment, more total interest) and a shorter one?

label: Product type rationale given
description: Did the adviser explain why the recommended product type — fixed, tracker, discounted or variable — suits this customer's circumstances and attitude to payment risk?

label: End of initial rate period and payment shock explained
description: Did the adviser explain what happens when the initial fixed or discounted period ends — that the rate reverts, that the payment will change, and that the customer will need to review? Leaving a customer unaware of the reversion is a leading cause of later complaints.

label: Recommendation explicitly linked to stated needs
description: Did the adviser explicitly justify the specific recommendation against the needs and circumstances the customer had stated earlier in the call?

label: Alternatives considered and rejection explained
description: Did the adviser reference alternatives that were considered and briefly explain why they were not recommended, rather than presenting a single option with no comparison?

label: Product transfer versus remortgage compared
description: On a remortgage or rate review, did the adviser compare staying with the existing lender (product transfer) against moving, including the cost and effort of each? Mark not applicable on a new purchase.

label: Total cost of borrowing explained, not just the monthly payment
description: Did the adviser explain the overall cost — total interest over the term or the true cost over the deal period — rather than presenting only the monthly payment? A cheap monthly payment that hides a high total cost is a fair value failure.

label: Early repayment charges explained
description: Did the adviser explain any early repayment charge: that it exists, roughly how much it is, and for how long it applies?

label: Product, valuation and legal fees explained
description: Did the adviser explain the other costs of the transaction — arrangement or product fee, valuation, legal or conveyancing costs — and whether any are added to the loan?

label: Overpayments and portability explained where material
description: Where relevant to this customer, did the adviser explain overpayment allowances and whether the product is portable if they move?

label: Affordability affirmatively checked
description: Did the adviser check with the customer that the recommended payment is genuinely affordable and sustainable, rather than assuming affordability from the lender's calculator alone?

label: Affordability at a higher rate discussed
description: Did the adviser discuss what would happen to the payment if interest rates rose — a stress or what-if conversation rather than presenting the current payment as fixed forever?

label: Vulnerability screened and responded to
description: Did the adviser identify indicators of vulnerability — health, bereavement, financial stress, low capability or understanding, time pressure — and respond appropriately? A cue raised by the customer must be acknowledged and acted on, not passed over (FG21/1).

label: Protection need raised
description: Did the adviser raise the customer's protection position alongside the mortgage — what would happen to the mortgage on death, serious illness or loss of income? Credit is for raising and exploring the need, not for making a sale.

label: Buildings insurance requirement mentioned
description: Did the adviser mention that buildings insurance will be required as a condition of the mortgage?

label: Understanding checked and questions invited
description: Did the adviser check that the customer had understood the recommendation and its costs, and invite questions — rather than asking a closed "does that all make sense?" and moving on?

label: Next steps, timescales and documentation explained
description: Did the adviser explain what happens next, the likely timescales, and that the customer will receive written illustration and suitability documentation?

label: No pressure or false urgency
description: Was the recommendation given without high-pressure tactics or manufactured urgency? Genuine, factual deadlines (a rate withdrawal already announced by the lender, an agreed completion date) are acceptable; invented scarcity is not.

label: Consent to proceed and credit search obtained
description: Before proceeding to application, did the adviser explain that a credit search will be carried out and obtain the customer's clear agreement to proceed? Consent must be explicit and must not be inferred.
